senses.gloss:
Bhoja, Bhojaka (IE 8-2; EI 1; 27; HD; LL), a Jāgīrdār; title of a feudatory; cf. the feminine form Bhojikī; also Mahā-bhoja. See Ep. Ind., Vol. I, p. 5.
 (EI 3; CII 3), a priest; title of a class of priests.
 Cf. Tamil pośar (SITI), one who enjoys a thing; the possessor.

bhojana-ākṣayiṇī, bhojan-ākṣayiṇī^1 (EI 32), a permanent endowment created for the maintenance of the donee; cf. akṣayanīvī, grāmagrāsa, etc.
[1] Correction submitted by Jim Funderburk on 20160315. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/CORRECTIONS/issues/252. note: ? Bojana+akzayiRI. Note change 'ya' to 'yi'.
bhojana-śālā (EI 23), an almshouse; a free-feeding house. Cf. sattra.
Bhojikī (LL), wife of a Bhojaka (q. v.). cf. Mahābhojī.
Bhojpurī, language and people of the Bhojpur Pargana of the Shahabad District of Bihar and the adjoining regions.
